source: FifthRow AI Agent Orchestration Enterprise Playbook April 2026
summary: Enterprise-level guide on scaling multi-agent orchestration: governance, compliance (EU AI Act), cross-agent coordination. 57% of orgs now deploy multi-step agent workflows in production.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — focuses on enterprise governance/compliance overlay, not orchestration architecture. AgentForge's current gap set is at the implementation level, not the governance layer.

source: Andrej Karpathy Loopy Era / AutoResearch (No Priors Interview 2026)
summary: Karpathy describes stopping manual coding and instead directing AI agents continuously ('loopy era'). AutoResearch project demonstrates fully autonomous experiment-train-evaluate cycles without human intervention.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AutoResearch's continuous autonomous loop mirrors AgentForge's auto-dispatch concept (HID-72). The 'loopy era' framing validates AgentForge's architectural direction. No specific new gap exposed.

source: LangGraph 1.0 GA + per-node timeouts + durable streaming (2026)
summary: LangGraph 1.0 GA (Oct 2025), Q2 2026 additions: per-node timeouts, durable streaming, graph-based state persistence. 34% of agent-framework citations in enterprise production docs.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — SSE streaming already shipped in AgentForge. Per-node timeouts would require runtime refactor tracked conceptually under HID-167 (retry/failure classification). No new gap.

summary: CrewAI 1.14 introduces pluggable memory/knowledge/RAG backends and Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol support for inter-agent communication.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses a fixed sequential state machine with no dynamic agent-to-agent routing. A2A protocol is relevant only if parallel/dynamic routing is adopted, which is explicitly deferred.

summary: AutoGen v1.0 GA reaches production readiness with event-driven multi-agent architecture. Microsoft's strategic focus shifting to broader Microsoft Agent Framework.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — Event-driven architecture is architecturally incompatible with AgentForge's deterministic sequential state machine. Microsoft's direction diverges from AgentForge's CLI-subprocess model.

source: MAGMA / MemRL — Multi-Graph Agentic Memory Architecture (2026)
summary: MemRL trains agents to selectively write to episodic memory via reinforcement signals (storing memories from successful outcomes). MAGMA achieves highest LoCoMo score of 0.7. Cross-session temporal query improvements of +29.6 points.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — Directly relevant to run-outcome episodic memory, which is already tracked by open issue HID-188. MemRL's selective-write approach could strengthen HID-188's implementation design.

source: DeerFlow 2.0 by ByteDance — Open-Source SuperAgent Harness (March 2026)
summary: DeerFlow 2.0 (ground-up rewrite on LangGraph) is an open-source superagent harness orchestrating sub-agents, persistent memory, sandboxed filesystem, extensible skills, and message gateways. GitHub Trending #1 on launch.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — DeerFlow's skills system and lead-agent-spawning-subagents pattern validates AgentForge's architecture. The harness-level memory (cross-session preferences + project context) is the main differentiator. Backlog full, no new gap.

source: Escher-Loop: Mutual Evolution by Closed-Loop Self-Referential Optimization (ICML 2026)
summary: Framework co-evolving Task Agents (problem solvers) and Optimizer Agents (that recursively refine task agents). Uses empirical win-loss signals for optimizer scoring. Accepted ICML 2026 AI4Math Workshop.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — Requires RL training loops and co-evolutionary infrastructure. Explicitly disqualified by the red flag list (RL training loops). Mathematical optimization domain doesn't transfer to code orchestration directly.

source: CODESKILL: Learning Self-Evolving Skills for Coding Agents (arXiv 2605.25430, May 2026)
summary: RL-based framework that extracts multi-granularity procedural skills from coding-agent trajectories, evolves skills with new experience, and maintains a compact skill bank. SOTA on SWE-Bench Verified and Terminal-Bench 2.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — Directly relevant to AgentForge's skill distillation system (distillationAgent.ts, agentSkillRepository.ts). However, the RL feedback loop requires infrastructure AgentForge doesn't have yet (HID-163 for telemetry needed first).

source: Darwin Gödel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents (ICLR 2026)
summary: Self-referential system where coding agents modify their own code and validate changes empirically via benchmarks, growing an archive of diverse high-quality agent variants inspired by Darwinian evolution.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — Self-modification of agent code is architecturally incompatible with AgentForge's static CLI-subprocess model and deterministic state machine. Would require full agent architecture rewrite.

source: Harrison Chase 'Agentic Map-Reduce' and Long-Horizon Agents (LangChain, 2026)
summary: Harrison Chase coins 'agentic map-reduce' for deterministic parallel subagent spawning. 2026 framed as 'first year of long-horizon agents' that plan, remember, and adapt over time. LangChain Memory Store for low-level persistent memory control.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — Long-horizon planning validates AgentForge's multi-stage state machine. Agentic map-reduce maps to potential parallel stage execution, but parallel execution is explicitly deferred. Memory Store pattern is already covered by skill distillation.

source: Skill-SD: Skill-Conditioned Self-Distillation for Multi-turn LLM Agents (arXiv 2604.10674, April 2026)
summary: Framework conditioning agent behavior on distilled procedural skills, enabling self-distillation from execution traces for multi-turn agents. Validated on coding and tool-use benchmarks.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — Confirms the value of injecting procedural skills into agent prompts. The executor skill injection gap (planner gets skills, executor doesn't) would benefit from this pattern. But this gap is conceptually within HID-188 scope and backlog is full.

summary: Karpathy defines 'agentic engineering' as the serious discipline that grows on top of vibe coding — raising the ceiling on software quality via systematic AI orchestration. Software 3.0 thesis: programs written through prompts, context, agents, tools, memory, and verification.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — Validates AgentForge's orchestration philosophy but offers no specific implementable pattern. Conceptual alignment, not an actionable gap.
